question: Why did repeat purchases decline?
step_1_intent_classification: Multi-Step Root-Cause Investigation: Customer Retention & Repeat Purchase Decline

step_2_identified_kpi.name: Customer Repeat Purchase Rate %
step_2_identified_kpi.formula_description: Percentage of unique customers (customer_unique_id) placing 2 or more orders.
step_2_identified_kpi.sql_expression: ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN total_orders >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2)

step_4_executed_sql_queries:
SELECT
            CASE
                WHEN acquisition_cohort_ym BETWEEN '2017-01' AND '2017-06' THEN '2017-H1 (Early Cohorts)'
                WHEN acquisition_cohort_ym BETWEEN '2017-07' AND '2017-12' THEN '2017-H2 (Mid Cohorts)'
                WHEN acquisition_cohort_ym BETWEEN '2018-01' AND '2018-08' THEN '2018-H1/Q3 (Recent Cohorts)'
                ELSE 'Other'
            END AS cohort_period,
            COUNT(*) AS unique_customers,
            SUM(is_repeat_customer) AS repeat_customers,
            ROUND(100.0 * SUM(is_repeat_customer) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS repeat_rate_pct,
            ROUND(AVG(lifetime_payment_brl), 2) AS avg_ltv_brl,
            ROUND(AVG(avg_customer_review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
            ROUND(100.0 * AVG(ever_had_late_delivery), 2) AS late_delivery_exposure_pct
        FROM vw_customer_summary
        WHERE acquisition_cohort_ym BETWEEN '2017-01' AND '2018-08'
        GROUP BY 1
        ORDER BY 1

SELECT
            ever_had_late_delivery,
            COUNT(*) AS customers_count,
            SUM(is_repeat_customer) AS repeat_customers,
            ROUND(100.0 * SUM(is_repeat_customer) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS repeat_rate_pct,
            ROUND(AVG(avg_customer_review_score), 2) AS avg_review_score,
            ROUND(AVG(lifetime_payment_brl), 2) AS avg_ltv_brl
        FROM vw_customer_summary
        GROUP BY ever_had_late_delivery
        ORDER BY ever_had_late_delivery

WITH cust_seq AS (
            SELECT
                c.customer_unique_id,
                o.order_purchase_timestamp,
                MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id) AS first_ts,
                MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id) AS last_ts,
                COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id) AS n_orders
            FROM olist_orders_dataset o
            JOIN olist_customers_dataset c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
        )
        SELECT
            COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS repeat_customers_total,
            ROUND(AVG(JULIANDAY(last_ts) - JULIANDAY(first_ts)), 1) AS avg_days_between_first_and_last_order,
            SUM(CASE WHEN (JULIANDAY(last_ts) - JULIANDAY(first_ts)) <= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS repeat_within_30d_rows,
            SUM(CASE WHEN (JULIANDAY(last_ts) - JULIANDAY(first_ts)) > 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS repeat_after_30d_rows
        FROM (
            SELECT DISTINCT customer_unique_id, first_ts, last_ts
            FROM cust_seq
            WHERE n_orders >= 2
        )

WITH cust_cat AS (
            SELECT
                customer_unique_id,
                MIN(product_category_english) AS primary_category,
                COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_count
            FROM vw_fact_order_items
            GROUP BY customer_unique_id
        )
        SELECT
            primary_category,
            COUNT(*) AS customers_count,
            SUM(CASE WHEN orders_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS repeat_customers,
            ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN orders_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS repeat_rate_pct
        FROM cust_cat
        GROUP BY primary_category
        HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000
        ORDER BY repeat_rate_pct DESC
        LIMIT 10

step_6_statistical_test_results.recommended_test: Two-way Chi-Square Test of Independence (2017-H1 vs. 2018 Acquisition Cohorts)

step_7_verified_root_causes.driver: 1. Right-Censoring / Observation Window Truncation (Observational Olist Fact)
step_7_verified_root_causes.evidence: Repeat buyers take an average of 87.3 days between their first and last order (1,541 of 2,997 repeat buyers repurchase >30 days later). 2017-H1 cohorts had 14-20 months of observation window (5.20% repeat rate), whereas 2018 cohorts were truncated by the dataset cutoff in August/October 2018 (2.14% repeat rate, Chi2=384.61, p=1.23e-85).

step_7_verified_root_causes.driver: 2. First-Order Late Delivery & Q1-2018 Carrier Congestion Spike (Observational Olist Fact)
step_7_verified_root_causes.evidence: In 2018-Q1/H1, late-delivery exposure rose to 9.32% (vs. 4.78% in 2017-H1), depressing average customer review scores on late orders from 4.29 to 2.57 stars and eroding post-purchase trust.

step_7_verified_root_causes.driver: 3. Category Mix Shift Toward Durable One-Off Purchases (Observational Olist Fact)
step_7_verified_root_causes.evidence: High-repeat categories such as bed_bath_table, sports_leisure, and furniture_decor exhibit 3.5%-4.5% repeat rates, whereas fast-growing 2018 categories (watches_gifts, auto, electronics) have <2.0% repeat rates.
